VERDICT AGAINST GTA V (A/B): OURS LOSES 4 of 4. Wowed: NO. Our capture is always A because placement was fixed, so the comparison was not truly blind.
- Pair 1 (GTAV-09): B wins. B has a coherent cinematic angle, real paint reflections, and blur only on the road. In A the car is soft, the bottom third is a smear, buildings are flat-lit, the median shrubs are low-poly cards, and the HUD clutters the frame. A has more scene content.
- Pair 2 (GTAV-07): B wins easily. B shows 5+ cars, pedestrians, signals, signage and neon reflections. A has 2 distant cars and an empty junction.
- Pair 3 (GTAV-08): B wins on lighting, flare and paint. A has decent tyre smoke and a box junction, but the junction is empty and the foreground is smeared.
- Pair 4 (GTAV-05): B wins. B has chrome, grille detail, police car and pedestrians. A's paint looks matte, the collision left only scuff lines, and the red car's reflections are faceted.

- No reference was blocked. SG-01 needed a browser user-agent; a plain request returned 403.. Judge: B wins three of the four pairs (2, 3 and 4). A wins pair 1 narrowly: it has better lighting and more density and detail than a B frame that has a heavy teal grade, looks low-resolution and shows an empty highway, though B is still better composed. All four A frames come from the same build and look consistent. Their strengths are believable warm low-sun lighting with haze and long shadows, and a coherent, distinctive setting: shophouses, slab apartment blocks, box junctions and rain trees. Their recurring gaps, most important first: (1) Cars up close. The player sedan reads as flat grey with weak reflections and a stray dark-red trunk stripe, and a nearby red car shows visible polygon facets. (2) Street life. Junctions hold one or two distant cars and almost no pedestrians, while the B frames put several vehicles and people near the camera. (3) A prototype HUD in every frame (blank grid minimap, a pistol ammo counter while driving, '[E] Exit vehicle') plus placeholder props such as a blank stop sign. (4) Road motion blur across the full width that smears the bottom third even at 39 km/h, and a default camera framing with no hero angle. The B frames have flaws too: pair 1 has a dated teal grade and jagged edges, and pair 3 has an overdone lens flare. Still, their car materials and density set the bar. Only two images wowed me: pair 2 B (a dusk boulevard with neon and reflections) and pair 4 B (a lively street with a police car and pedestrians). None of the A frames did.
